{[—What is the point of research carried out by biz schools?][371040]} {[Students go to universities and other academic institutions to prepare for their future.][371052]} {[We pay tuition and struggle through classes in the hopes that we can find a fulfilling and exciting career.][371066]} {[But the choice of your university has a large influence on your future.][371085]} {[How can you know which university will prepare you the best for your future?][371098]} {[Like other academic institutions, busi­ness schools are judged by the quality of the research carried out by their faculties.][371113]} {[Professors must both teach students and also produce original research in their own field.][371133]} {[The quality of this research is assessed by academic publications.][371148]} {[At the same time, universities have another responsibility to equip their students for the real world, however that is defined.][371160]} {[Most students learning from professors will not go into academics themselves—so how do academics best prepare them for their future careers, whatever that may be?][371181]} {[Whether academic research actually produces anything that is useful to the practice of business, or even whether it is its job to do so, are questions that can provoke vigorous arguments on campus.][371208]} {[The debate, which first flared during the 1950s, was reignited in August, when AACSB Interna­tional, the most widely recognised global accrediting agency for business schools, announced it would consider changing the way it evaluates research.][371241]} {[The news followed rather damning criti­cism in 2002 from Jeffrey Pfefler, a Stanford professor, and Christina Fong of Washington Uni­versity, which questioned whether business education in its current guise was sustainable.][371277]} {[The study found that traditional modes of academia were not adequately preparing students for the kind of careers they faced in current times.][371308]} {[The most controversial recommendation in AACSB’s draft report (which was sent round to administrators for their comment) is that the schools should be required to demonstrate the value of their faculties’ research not simply by listing its citations in journals, but by demonstrating the impact it has on the professional world.][371332]} {[1-7 New qualifiers, such as average incomes, student placement in top firms and business collaborations, would now be considered just as important as academic publications.][371387]} {[AACSB justifies its stance by saying that it wants schools and faculty to play to their strengths, whether they be in pedagogy, in the research of practical applications, or in scholarly endeavor.][371411]} {[Traditionally, universities operate in a pyramid structure.][371444]} {[Everyone enters and stays in an attempt to be successful in their academic field.][371451]} {[A psychology professor must publish competi­tive research in the top neuroscience journals.][371465]} {[A Cultural Studies professor must send graduate students on new field research expeditions to be taken seriously.][371477]} {[This research is the core of a university’s output.][371494]} {[And research of any kind is expensive—AACSB points out that business schools in America alone spend more than $320m a year on it.][371503]} {[So it seems legitimate to ask "for what purpose is it undertaken? "][371527]}

{[If a school chose to specialise in professional outputs rather than academic outputs, it could use such a large sum of money and redirect it into more fruitful programs.][371542]} {[For example, if a business school wanted a larger presence of employees at top financial firms, this money may be better spent on a career center which focuses on building the skills of students, rather than paying for more high-level research to be done through the effort of faculty.][371570]} {[A change in evaluation could also open the door to inviting more professionals from different fields to teach as adjuncts.][371620]} {[Stu­dents could take accredited courses from people who are currently working in their dream field.][371640]} {[The AACSB insists that universities answer the question as to why research is the most critical component of traditional education.][371656]} {[On one level, the question is simple to answer.][371677]} {[Research in business schools, as anywhere else, is about expanding the boundaries of knowledge; it thrives on answering unasked questions.][371687]} {[Surely this pursuit of knowledge is still important to the university system.][371708]} {[Our society progresses because we learn how to do things in new ways, a process which depends heavily on research and academics.][371721]} {[But one cannot ignore the other obvious practical uses of research publications.][371743]} {[Research is also about cementing schools’ and professors’ reputations.][371756]} {[Schools gain kudos from their faculties’ record of publication: which journals publish them, and how often.][371766]} {[In some cases, such as with government-funded schools in Britain, it can affect how much money they receive.][371783]} {[10-12 For professors, the mantra is often “publish or perish”.][371802]} {[Their careers depend on being seen in the right journals.][371811]} {[But at a certain point, one has to wonder whether this research is being done for the benefit of the university or for the students the university aims to teach.][371822]} {[Greater publications will attract greater funding, which will in turn be spent on better publications.][371853]} {[Students seeking to enter pro­fessions out of academia find this cycle frustrating, and often see their professors as being part of the “Ivory Tower” of academia, operating in a self-contained community that has little influ­ence on the outside world.][371869]} {[The research is almost universally unread by real-world managers.][371908]} {[Part of the trouble is that the journals labour under a similar ethos.][371918]} {[They publish more than 20,000 articles each year.][371931]} {[Most of the research is highly quantitative, hypothesis-driven and esoteric.][371940]} {[As a result, it is almost univer­sally unread by real-world managers.][371952]} {[Much of the research criticises other published research.][371962]} {[A paper in a 2006 issue of Strategy & Leadership commented that “research is not designed with managers’ needs in mind, nor is it communicated in the journals they read.][371971]} {[For the most part, it has become a self-referential closed system irrelevant to corporate performance.][372000]} {[” The AACSB demands that this segregation must change for the future of higher education.][372015]} {[If students must invest thousands of dollars for an education as part of their career path, the academics which serve the students should be more fully incorporated into the professional world.][372031]} {[This means that uni­versities must focus on other strengths outside of research, such as professional networks, tech­nology skills, and connections with top business firms around the world.][372062]} {[Though many universi­ties resisted the report, today’s world continues to change.][372090]} {[The universities which prepare students for our changing future have little choice but to change with new trends and new standards.][372102]}

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 1 - 3:

Choose the correct letter A, B, C or D.
Write the correct letter in boxes 1-3 on your answer sheet.

options.text: to focus on listing research paper’s citation only.
to consider the quantity of academic publications.
to evaluate how the paper influences the field.
to maintain the traditional modes of academia.

questions.explanationHtml:
C
 
controversial (a) gây tranh cãi
influence = impact: sự ảnh hưởng, tác động
paper = research
Các trường kinh tế theo đề nghị mới nhất của hiệp hội AACSB phải chứng minh được giá trị của các bài nghiên cứu của họ bằng cách thể hiện sự ảnh hưởng của nó lên chính lĩnh vực kinh doanh đó.

options.text: to give full play to the faculties’ advantage.
to reinforce the play to the pyramid structure of universities.
to push professors to publish competitive papers.
to reduce costs of research in universities.

questions.explanationHtml:
A
 
justify (n) đưa ra lí lẽ cho cái gì đó
play to their strengths = give full play to the faculties' advantage
ACCSB đã đưa ra lí do cho việc thay đổi cách đánh giá các trường kinh tế là vì họ muốn các trường này phải chơi theo thế mạnh của họ theo nhiều khía cạnh: "pedagogy" - sư phạm, "practical applications" - ứng dụng thực tiễn, và "scholarly endeavor" - nghiên cứu khoa học (thiên về viết báo, sách, ...)

options.text: to characterize research as irrelevant to company performance
to suggest that managers don’t read research papers.
to describe students’ expectation for universities.
to exemplify high-quality research papers.

questions.explanationHtml:
A
 
Tác giả chỉ ra rằng những nghiên cứu trong lĩnh vực kinh doanh đa số là không được đọc bởi những nhà quản lí thực thụ trên thế giới. Và bài báo Strategy and Leadership cũng chỉ ra điều đó, nói rằng: nghiên cứu không được thiết kế dành cho các nhà quản lí, vì đa phần các bài nghiên cứu đều nằm trong 1 hệ thống khép kín, "irrelevant" - không liên quan đến "corporate performance" - sự thành công, hiệu quả của doanh nghiệp.

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 4 - 5:

Choose TWO letters, A-E.
Write the correct letters in boxes 4-5 on your answer sheet.

questions.text:
Questions 4 - 5:
Choose TWO letters, A-E.Write the correct letters in boxes 4-5 on your answer sheet.

options.text: Students should pay less to attend universities.
Business education is not doing their job well.
Professors should not focus on writing papers.
Students are ill-prepared for their career from universities.
Recognized accrediting agency can evaluate research well.

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 6 - 10:

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 3?
In boxes 6-10 on your answer sheet, write

TRUE                if the statement is true

FALSE              if the statement is false

NOT GIVEN     if the information is not given in the passage

options.text: TRUE
FALSE
NOT GIVEN

questions.text: The debate about the usefulness of academic research for business practices is a recent one.
questions.explanationHtml:
FALSE
 
flare (v) nhen nhóm xuất hiện
debate (n) tranh luận
"The debate" ở đây chính là cuộc tranh luận về việc nghiên cứu học thuật, đặc biệt trong lĩnh vực kinh doanh có thực sự hiệu quả - "useful" cho ứng dụng thực tiễn hay không, đã nhen nhóm từ những năm 1950, CHỨ KHÔNG PHẢI gần đây - "recent"

questions.text: AACSB’s draft report was not reviewed externally.
questions.explanationHtml:
FALSE
 
"AACSB’s draft report was not reviewed externally" --> Bản nháp báo cáo của AACSB không được người ngoài xem qua - "reviewed externally" LÀ FALSE vì nó được gửi cho các "administrators" - quản trị viên để lấy bình luận của họ.

questions.text: Business schools in the US spend more than 320 million dollars yearly on research.
questions.explanationHtml:
8
TRUE
Câu hỏi: "Business schools in the US spend more than 320 million dollars yearly on research"
a year = yearly
Câu hỏi hoàn toàn khớp với thông tin trong đoạn "And research of any kind is expensive—AACSB points out that business schools in America alone spend more than $320m a year on it"

NOT GIVEN
 
"Many universities pursue professional outputs." --> Nhiều trường đại học chọn theo đuổi những sản phẩm chuyên môn LÀ NOT GIVEN vì trong bài chỉ đề cập thông tin một trường có thể chọn "specialise" - đặc biệt theo đuổi sản phẩm chuyên môn, điều này không có nghĩa là nhiều trường đều chọn cái này, từ làm cho câu này "not given" chính là từ "many".

questions.text: Greater publications benefit professors and students as well.
questions.explanationHtml:
FALSE
 
"Greater publications benefit professors and students as well." --> Việc xuất bản các bài báo nghiên cứu khoa học có lợi cho cả giáo sư và sinh viên LÀ FALSE vì theo thông tin trong bài, điều này chỉ có lợi cho giáo sư và nhà trường trong việc củng cố danh tiếng - "cementing reputations" và nhận tiền - "receive money". Việc xuất bản các bài nghiên cứu khoa học nhiều hơn chỉ mang lại nhiều "funding" - trợ cấp hơn và số tiền này cũng lại được tiếp tục chi cho nghiên cứu khoa học. Nhiều sinh viên bước chân vào lĩnh vực kinh doanh chuyên nghiệp cảm thấy vòng lặp lẩn quẩn này rất phiền toái và thường xem cái giáo sư là "Ivory Tower" - tháp ngà, một điều gì đó chỉ hoạt động trong cộng đồng khép kín và có rất ít sự ảnh hưởng lên thế giới thực bên ngoài.

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 11 - 14:

Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A-E, below.

Write the correct letter, A-E, in boxes 11-14 on your answer sheet.

A          it progresses as we learn innovative ways of doing things.
B          the trends and standards are changing.
C          their jobs depend on it.
D          they care about their school rankings and government funds.
E          it helps students to go into top business firms.
